chose: conjectures view lists resolve().open over the WHOLE model, ignoring any active stream scope
over: filtering the open list to the surfed stream
because: the masthead count that invites the drill-in is unscoped — a list showing fewer entries than the number that advertised it would read as a bug, and resolve() already owns the open/answered judgment

chose: the cell-windowing block was factored out of the timeline branch into windowCells and shared
over: a parallel copy of the anchor/reserve/span logic for the conjectures list
because: the edge-only sliding and the reserved 'older' line are one mechanism with subtle invariants (never slice a cell, honest below-count) — two copies would drift apart at exactly the corner cases the comments exist to guard

chose: conjecture cells are timelineCell plus an optional one-line hint, discriminator FIRST then candidates
over: candidates before the discriminator, mirroring the detail view's order
because: reusing the cell keeps the two lists visually one system, and the discriminator is the actionable field — the hint clips right-to-left, so the one thing the ellipsis must never eat goes first

chose: the entry drill-in remembers WHERE it was opened from (ui.back) and esc returns there
over: esc always returning to the timeline
because: a reader scanning the open list drills into one question mid-scan; dumping them back on the timeline discards their position in the list they were actually reading

chose: keybinding: both c and o open the conjectures view from the timeline
because: the masthead says OPEN conjecture(s) — either word a reader reaches for should land; both keys were free
